name: EthOS VM Manager
description: Run Windows and Linux virtual machines on this NAS with hardware acceleration. Create a VM from an ISO or boot a ready-made system image such as the EthOS OS release, use it from the browser console, and let it start again with EthOS.
author: SyncHot
changelog: 1.0.9: Console links point at the right port again. The window asked EthOS for the console's published host port through a variable that does not exist (`_ctx` instead of `ctx`), the error was swallowed by a try/catch, and every link fell back to the container port 8094 — on the NAS that number belongs to another service, so Console opened a dead or foreign page. The lookup now uses `ctx`, retries while Docker republishes the mapping, and refuses to build a URL out of the container port: if the port is not published yet it says so instead of opening a broken link. 1.0.8: the console opens in a new tab when EthOS is served over https — browsers drop an http iframe inside an https page as mixed content, which looked like a blank console with no error. On http (LAN) the console still embeds, and the panel says which mode it used. 1.0.7: picking a bootable image (.img/.img.xz/.qcow2) now pre-selects UEFI firmware and explains why, so an EthOS OS image boots on the first try. 1.0.6: boot a ready-made image, not just an installer — pick a .img/.img.xz/.qcow2 file (for example the EthOS OS release) and it becomes the VM's disk, decompressed and converted to qcow2 in one step, with a free-space check up front. .iso installers still attach as CD-ROM. 1.0.5: the window shows a calm “Starting engine…” state while the first-run QEMU/noVNC installation is still running, instead of a connection-reset error. 1.0.4: the console no longer reserves host port 8094 — Docker maps the container port to a free host port and the window discovers it, so the package starts even when another service already uses 8094. 1.0.3: requires EthOS 2.0. 1.0.2: the console overlay no longer covers the window — it is hidden until you press Console, so the machine list and the create form are always visible. 1.0.1: the browser console connects again — the WebSocket handshake now selects the `binary` subprotocol noVNC asks for, which browsers otherwise reject. Port 8094 shows a short explanation instead of raw JSON when opened directly, the create form pre-fills a real storage root, and picking a folder fills the ISO list automatically. 1.0.0: first release. KVM virtual machines with a browser console: create a VM from an ISO stored on the NAS, start, stop and reset it, follow its live status, and let it start automatically with EthOS. Disks are qcow2 files on a share you pick. Snapshots, cloning and OVA export follow in 1.1.
